evals.name: wire-bounded-context
evals.prompt: Wire a modular-monolith user context with HTTP inbound adapters, a PostgreSQL repository, and an outbox publisher.
evals.expected_output: Composition-root wiring that keeps domain ports inward and adapters outward.
assertions: The domain does not import HTTP, PostgreSQL, or messaging libraries.
Ports are owned by the consuming core layer and adapters satisfy them.
Construction happens at the composition root or module boundary.

evals.name: anti-corruption-layer
evals.prompt: The Order bounded context needs user contact details from the User bounded context. How should they communicate?
evals.expected_output: Cross-context communication via an explicit Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL), caller-owned port, DTOs, and boundary adapter.
assertions: Order context does not directly import User domain entities.
An outbound port interface is defined in Order context representing the needed user data.
An adapter translates between User external data and Order-owned DTOs or domain types.
The Order usecase does not import User domain entities directly.

evals.name: reject-inward-dependency
evals.prompt: A developer places SQL queries and pgx driver calls directly inside an internal/user/service domain struct. Fix the architecture.
evals.expected_output: Refactoring that extracts repository interface in domain and moves pgx implementation to outbound/repository/db adapter.
assertions: Extracts persistence interface into domain port.
Moves all SQL and driver code into adapter package.
Ensures domain package imports zero infrastructure libraries.
